candidates.title: MUXQ: Mixed-to-Uniform Precision MatriX Quantization via Low-Rank Outlier Decomposition
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have achieved outstanding performance across a wide range of natural language processing tasks, but their enormous parameter counts impose ubstantial memory and computational overheads. This challenge is particularly critical in NPU-based on-device environments, where FP16/FP32 computation is inefficient and integer (INT) quantization is therefore essential. However, existing methods, including ZeroQuant, LLM.int8(), and SmoothQuant, do not fully address input-activation outliers and the associated hardware inefficiencies. To overcome these limitations, we propose MUXQ (Mixed-to-Uniform Quantization). MUXQ detects outlier channels in input activations and introduces a small auxiliary matrix that redistributes outlier magnitudes across channels, thereby alleviating the outlier problem. This enables even activation outliers to be quantized at low-precision INT levels while preserving a hardware-friendly computation structure. Experiments on GPT-2 models at three scales (0.1B, 0.3B, and 0.7B parameters) using the WikiText-2 dataset show that MUXQ consistently achieves lower perplexity than naive quantization. In particular, under per-tensor quantization, MUXQ quantizes both activations and weights to INT8 while maintaining accuracy close to that of FP16. With only modest computational overhead, MUXQ enables stable low-precision inference and can be readily combined with other quantization techniques. These results suggest that MUXQ provides a promising direction for efficient and accurate LLM inference on edge devices.
candidates.reason: 要旨ではNPUベースのオンデバイス環境向けに、入力活性化の外れ値チャネルを低ランク分解して混合精度を均一精度へ変換する行列量子化MUXQを提案しており、オンデバイス推論向け量子化への直接貢献が確認できる。

candidates.title: When 1+1 Backfires: Rethinking Relevance-Diversity Balancing for Sample-Aware Visual Token Reduction
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 34th ACM International Conference on Multimedia
candidates.abstract: Visual token compression has emerged as a critical technique for reducing the inference cost of Vision-Language Models. Existing methods select tokens based on text relevance, visual diversity, or a fixed combination of both---treating the relevance-diversity balance as a universal constant independent of the input. We conduct a systematic analysis to challenge this assumption. At the dataset level, grid-searching the optimal relevance-diversity weight per benchmark reveals substantial cross-task variation. More critically, we further maximize per-sample answer likelihood to recover sample-level oracle weights, finding that their distributions not only differ markedly across benchmarks but also exhibit high within-benchmark variance. Based on these observations, we propose SAVER, a framework for Sample-Aware relevance-diversity balanced Visual tokEn Reduction. We first derive a Geometric Intent Prior (GIP) from the spatial concentration of text-relevant tokens to infer a sample-specific relevance-diversity weight, and then apply this weight to jointly select tokens via a Weighted Text Centroid (WTC) for relevance scoring and a Visual Marginal Coverage Gain (VMCG) for diversity. SAVER requires no additional training and achieves sample-aware balancing entirely at inference time. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SAVER consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across diverse benchmarks, retaining 96.5% of full-model performance on LLaVA-1.5-7B with only 11.1% of the original visual tokens, and further generalizing to LLaVA-NeXT and Mini-Gemini.
candidates.reason: 要旨では視覚言語モデルの推論コストを下げる視覚トークン削減について、関連性と多様性の重みがサンプルごとに異なることを示しサンプル適応型のバランス手法を検討しており、VLMのprefillトークン削減という推論効率化への直接貢献がある。

candidates.title: SHq: Learnable Grids for LLM Weight Quantization
candidates.abstract: Block-scaled lookup-table (LUT) formats, which represent weights as indices into a small value set (the grid), have become standard for low-bit LLM quantization, ranging from NF4 and BOF4 to the 3-bit LUT instruction in NVIDIA Rubin. While these formats leave the grid definition flexible, existing implementations rely on fixed grids derived either from numerical data types (INT, FP) or assumed weight distributions (NF, BOF). We demonstrate that no single fixed grid is universally optimal; the best fixed grid varies with bit-width: BOFS at 2 bits, NF at 4 and 5 bits, and INT at 6 bits. We introduce SHq, a closed-form family of grids parameterized by two critical degrees of freedom: a companding strength {\alpha} that interpolates level spacing from uniform to floating-point-like, and an offset c that introduces asymmetry. This offset allows the sign bit of the FP8 block scale, otherwise unused, to select between the grid and its mirror image, up to doubling the number of distinct values available per block. SHq modifies only the lookup table contents and serves as a drop-in replacement for the grid in any such format. Across five models ranging from 3B to 35B parameters, including a mixture-of-experts architecture, evaluated at 2-6 bits using RTN and GPTQ, SHq achieves the lowest KL divergence in every setting at 3 and 4 bits and in most settings at 2, 5 and 6 bits. It outperforms the best fixed grid by up to 34% and remains superior under mixed-precision configurations. At 4.5 bits per weight, the SHq format reduces the KL divergence of NVFP4 by 41-67% while improving downstream accuracy. Grid families incorporating both spacing and offset parameters perform comparably, whereas those lacking an offset exhibit clearly higher error, confirming that these two degrees of freedom drive the observed gains. We therefore propose SHq as the standard grid for block-scaled lookup-table formats.
candidates.reason: 要旨ではブロック スケールLUT形式の重み量子化について固定グリッドの限界を示し、2パラメータで閉形式に学習可能なグリッド族SHqを提案しており、低ビットLLM重み量子化への直接の技術的貢献が具体的に確認できる。

candidates.title: When Is High-Bandwidth Flash Cost-Effective for LLM Inference?
candidates.abstract: Can high-bandwidth flash (HBF) make LLM inference cheaper than adding GPUs? By storing weights closer to the GPU than SSD, HBF may reduce the number of GPUs needed for model capacity. However, this integration is only justified if it meets service targets and its cost is recovered. We simulate this integration using public component data across nine dense and mixture-of-experts (MoE) models, five workloads, two GPU platforms, and 1--100 GPUs. At fixed demand, HBF reduces the minimum GPU count to meet a service target in 98 of 468 comparisons; majority of them are paused and short sessions, 63 remain cost-effective at half a GPU price per HBF stack. For single short-chat users, HBF enables large MoEs, e.g. DeepSeek V3 and Kimi K2, to meet a relaxed service target on one RTX~4090 GPU, where conventional serving fails. At fixed GPU count, HBF improves throughput in 48\% of matched comparisons below 16 GPUs and 13\% at larger counts. Even at 100 RTX~4090-scale GPUs, cascaded HBF raises offline throughput by 16.4--26.5$\times$ for three large MoEs. We found savings and throughput gains arise in different scenarios.
candidates.reason: 要旨では高帯域フラッシュに重みを置く構成がGPU増設よりLLM推論を安くできる条件を、9モデル・5ワークロード・2GPU基盤でのシミュレーションで評価しており、推論基盤の計測・シミュレーションとして直接関係する。
